itemListElement.name: Where Should a Local Business Put Its First Marketing Dollars? A Practical Order of Operations

mainEntity.name: Where should a new local business spend its first marketing dollars?

acceptedAnswer.text: Start with what makes every other channel work: a verified Google Business Profile, accurate details and a habit of asking for and answering reviews. Those cost mostly time. Once you can answer every contact that arrives, add paid search, such as Local Services Ads or Google Ads, to reach people who are already searching.

mainEntity.name: Should a local service business start with Google Ads or Facebook ads?

acceptedAnswer.text: Search usually comes first, because the person searching already wants to hire someone. Social ads create awareness and work best once your profile, reviews and follow-up are ready to catch the attention they bring.

mainEntity.name: Is there a percentage of revenue I should spend on marketing?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no number we can verify, so we will not give one. The Intuit survey estimates an average small business advertising budget of about $78,000, but it spans businesses from zero to over 100 employees and is not a target. Work out your own budget from what a customer is worth to you and how many contacts you can actually handle.

mainEntity.name: Can I pay Google to rank higher in the map results?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Google says "There's no way to request or pay for a better local ranking on Google." Local rankings rest mainly on relevance, distance and popularity, which is why the profile and reviews are worth your time. Paid ads are a separate placement.
